name: MCP Server
rationale: MCP servers need a hard boundary between protocol transport, tool registration, and deterministic domain logic so stdio and hosted modes share behavior safely.

sources.label: Model Context Protocol architecture
sources.note: Rules are distilled from MCP server implementation constraints and this repo's local architecture contract.

directories.purpose: MCP tool registration, schemas, and response formatting.
Pure contract, review, intake, and stack-pack logic.

fileRules.name: Transport-neutral tools
fileRules.rule: MCP tool behavior should be reusable across stdio and hosted HTTP transports.
fileRules.trigger: A tool handler contains transport-specific request, response, or filesystem access logic.
fileRules.recommendation: Move transport concerns into src/http.ts, src/index.ts, or src/infrastructure and keep tool handlers focused on validation and response formatting.
fileRules.goodExample: Tool handler calls a domain function and returns a JSON MCP response.
fileRules.badExample: Tool handler reads arbitrary local paths or branches on HTTP headers.

fileRules.name: No hosted filesystem scanning
fileRules.rule: Hosted MCP mode must not expose tools that scan arbitrary server-local paths.
fileRules.trigger: Hosted server registers a local workspace scanning tool.
fileRules.recommendation: Disable local workspace tools in hosted mode and require clients to send file summaries.

moduleBoundaries: Transport entrypoints should create a server and connect a transport; they should not own domain logic.
Tool handlers may validate MCP input and format output, but domain modules should own decisions.
Hosted mode should accept client-provided file summaries instead of reading local server paths.
testingExpectations: Domain reviewers should have unit tests for false positives and real anti-monolith findings.
Hosted mode should have a smoke test that lists tools without exposing local-only tools.
agentInstructions: Keep stdio and hosted HTTP entrypoints thin.
Do not add persistence until a feature requires saved templates, audit history, billing, or teams.
